Hi Akira —

Thanks again for the great session last week. Attached is the draft case study (Acme_CaseStudy_Draft.pdf) based on the interview notes. Two quick asks so we can proceed with marketing in both EU and APAC: 

1) Permission to publish the case study and short testimonial quotes in English + translated versions (Japanese, Korean, German, French). We can either translate with your localization team or use our vetted vendor and send translations for your sign-off.

2) Confirmation we can publish the OmniHub logo and the 32% latency reduction stat (we can omit or redact any metric you prefer).

If useful, we can provide a short-quote variant for APAC channels (20–40 char snippets) and a longer EU-friendly version that includes the full metric with the appropriate privacy clause.

I've cc'd Marissa (marketing) who will coordinate localization and the consent flow. Attached: Acme_CaseStudy_Draft.pdf for review.

Would you be able to confirm preference (vendor vs internal translation) and any regional restrictions by next Tue, Aug 5?

Thanks —
Soojin

Hi Soojin —

Thanks for sending the draft. OmniHub is happy to be a reference; we like the write-up overall. A few regional notes from our side: 

- Japan: fine with publishing English and Japanese translations. We prefer Redwood to handle the translation and send back the JP text for final sign-off (helps keep consistency).
- Korea: can do Korean translations but marketing prefers short, punchy quotes rather than long paragraphs; please prepare a short-quote pack.
- EU (France/Germany): we need to check with our legal/compliance team before publishing any customer-identifying metrics in Germany. Claire (cc'd on this thread) is taking point for France and will loop in our DPO for DE.

On data retention: can you confirm how long Redwood will keep the signed consent and whether the case study will contain any PII beyond company name and anonymized usage metrics?

Akira

Hi Akira —

Really appreciate the quick response and the guidance for each region. Quick answers below and next steps: 

- Translations: Redwood can manage translations via our vendor (we will provide JP/KR/DE/FR drafts). We'll send the translated text back for your review and sign-off prior to publishing.
- Short-quote pack: noted for Korea — we'll prepare a 6–8 quote set optimized for social/ads.
- PII & retention: Redwood will only include company name and anonymized performance metrics (no personal names or emails). Signed consent forms are retained for auditing; standard retention is 7 years unless you request earlier deletion — happy to align with OmniHub policy.

Attached is a blank Consent_Form.docx and a suggested workflow (DocuSign link in the related links). If you'd like, we can populate the consent with the agreed metric redaction option (i.e., redact the 32% stat for Germany) before sending to signatures.

Next steps:
1) Akira / Claire confirm whether DE should have the metric redacted.
2) We prepare translations and short-quote pack and send for review.
3) Send Consent_Form via DocuSign for signature.

I'm cc'ing Vivek to flag marketing localization questions (APAC nuance), and I'll loop legal if Claire confirms DE restrictions.

Thanks —
Marissa

• For Japan we should avoid literal translations of idioms; we'll propose a JP-native variant.
• For Korea: focus on 2–3 short quotes (headline + subhead) — provide character-limited versions for banner/ad layouts.
• For translations, we can either: (A) use our vendor and have OmniHub approve, or (B) provide raw English + ask OmniHub to share their internal reviewer. Option A is faster.

I'll draft a simple localization matrix (Quote_Matrix.xlsx) showing quote length, channel, and language variant. I'll also flag any screenshots in the draft that may need localization or removal per local laws (JP prefers screenshots with anonymized IDs).

If Akira/Claire confirm redaction for Germany, we'll produce a DE-safe version and a full EN/JP/KR/FR variant.
